Imagine a workforce where scientists process data thousands of times faster, engineers design sustainable energy systems with superhuman precision, and policymakers forecast global threats with artificial intelligence-linked neural networks. A population devoid of illness would alleviate healthcare burdens (over 10% of global GDP is spent on healthcare), freeing capital for progress. Societal and Economic Imperatives

A cognitively and physically superior workforce could outperform unenhanced humans, boosting productivity, creativity, and risk mitigation. Companies could accelerate technological breakthroughs, from quantum computing to AI, while individual earnings and longevity-related consumer spending would soar. Comparatively, compulsory education was once contentious but is now universally accepted as foundational to progress; similarly, enhancements represent an ethical imperative to optimize human capacity for societal benefit.

To reject mandatory human enhancement is to choose stagnation over progress, suffering over cure, and fragmentation over unity. By embracing these technologies as a collective human project, we honor the spirit of innovation that elevated our species from caves to colonies on Mars.
